Container.Name: theseus-ai
Container.Overview:
Theseus AI - a local, deliberating multi-agent coding council that runs your own subscription-authenticated CLIs (Claude, Codex, Antigravity), not per-token API keys.
First run: 1. Start the container, then check its log for the dashboard URL - it carries a one-time login ticket. 2. Set AI_COUNCIL_TOKEN below to a secret of your choosing (openssl rand -hex 24) so that URL stays valid across restarts, then bookmark http://YOUR-UNRAID-IP:8760/?ticket=THE-SAME-SECRET - that is your permanent dashboard link. The bare WebUI button will show "Missing session token" by design; it is not a broken build, it is what a link with no ticket does. 3. Set AI_COUNCIL_ALLOWED_HOSTS to every hostname/IP you will actually browse to (your unraid IP, a .local name, a reverse-proxy domain). Requests claiming any other Host are rejected - this is a DNS-rebinding defence, and it is deliberately not permissive-by-default even though the socket itself is LAN-reachable. 4. Open Settings -> Agents inside the dashboard to install whichever CLIs you use (Claude, Codex, Antigravity) and sign them in - nothing is baked into the image, so their own updaters keep working exactly as on a bare-metal install. Do the same for GitHub under the connections card if you want the commit button to push.
The one volume (Appdata) is where all of that persists: the app's config, the installed CLIs, and their logins. Add further volumes for whichever working folder(s) you want the council editing.
Container.Description: A local, deliberating multi-agent coding council - Claude, Codex and Antigravity critique each other's answers before anything is written to disk.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: App config, installed agent CLIs, and their logins - everything that has to survive a restart.

Config.Name: Workspace
Config.Description: The working folder the council edits. Point the app at /workspace from its own folder picker. Add more Path entries for more than one project.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id files are written as - 99 is unraid's own 'nobody'.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id files are written as - 100 is unraid's own 'users'.

Config.Name: AI_COUNCIL_TOKEN
Config.Description: A secret of your own choosing (openssl rand -hex 24). Makes the dashboard URL survive a restart - see the Overview above. Leave blank and a one-time login is generated fresh on every start instead, readable from this container's log.

Config.Name: AI_COUNCIL_ALLOWED_HOSTS
Config.Description: Comma-separated hostnames/IPs you will browse to - your unraid IP, a .local name, a reverse-proxy domain. Required for the dashboard to accept any request that isn't loopback.
